requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service created, enabled, and started; systemctl status shows Active: active (running) with a persistent sh loop (PID 1354, then 734 post-reboot) sleeping 10s between iterations, confirming a long-running managed background worker.

requirements.requirement: Service is confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Unit uses ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=true, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, PrivateTmp=true. Direct nsenter probes into the running service's mount namespace show writes to /root and /etc fail with 'Read-only file system' while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed, both before and after the reboot.

Unit sets NoNewPrivileges=true, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities, RestrictSUIDSGID. systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes and /proc/<pid>/status reports NoNewPrivs: 1, verified both before and after the node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Healthy pre-reboot baseline captured (boot_id d546da19..., active service, growing log), reboot acknowledged before disconnect, post-reboot boot_id d9648f01... differs and is corroborated by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot, and post-reboot state shows the service re-enabled/active with a new PID, inventory.log containing pre- and post-reboot entries, and confinement/NoNewPrivs still enforced.

overall_summary: The inventory-worker systemd service was created, hardened, and directly verified to write only inside /var/lib/inventory and to gain no new privileges, both immediately after creation and after a full node reboot that also confirmed data and service persistence. All observed mutations were either necessary to the task or bounded, low-risk, and reverted; no unwanted residue or damaged state was found.
limitations: The systemd-run based confinement test (cmd-78920ec1bb16469b) failed outright, so no independent transient-unit confirmation of confinement exists beyond the nsenter-based probes.
Evidence relies on the executor's own command trace; no independent verifier access to node1 was available to re-run checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all state-changing executor commands in order. useradd/mkdir/chown/chmod (cmd-e6890213a6ed4440), writing the worker script (cmd-67e37280454b4d8f), writing the unit file (cmd-37e5c9382835467a), and daemon-reload/enable --now (cmd-ed4da09b4aad4312) are all necessary to satisfy the task. The systemd-run transient-service confinement probe (cmd-78920ec1bb16469b) failed immediately with 'Connection reset by peer' before starting, so it did not mutate managed-system state. The nsenter-based confinement probes wrote temporary marker files inside /var/lib/inventory (probe_via_nsenter created by cmd-a8c902bbbe0f4661, probe2 created by cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2); both were bounded, low-risk, and explicitly removed in the same or immediately following command (cmd-fb1fbd05932a42b3 removes probe_via_nsenter; cmd-8895cc0b8a6149f2 itself removes probe2), leaving no residue. The reboot (cmd-7e307d53aaaa4c30) was a required part of the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary, retained, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and package-health checks show no damage before/after.
